## Results

- Monte Carlo force-pairing over 239 decided cross-archetype games: melee wins 61.5%, but a list-level cluster bootstrap (13 lists, 2,000 resamples) puts the interval at [39.1, 82.1]. List identity, not archetype, drives the result
- Replay determinism: 0 desyncs across 1,535 recorded actions in six games, two of them played by humans
- Roster importer verified against 179 tournament lists: 0 of 9,190 models missing
- Bradley-Terry list ranking is stable across board settings
- Of three AI heuristics tested, only stratagem use moved outcomes: 54.6% [50.6, 58.6] over 600 seat-swapped games against a 50.7% control, with an inverted-objective control at 44.6% bounding the headroom
- 42 seeded, headless test suites; conformance testing found five implemented rules that no driver could reach and wired them in

## The problem

Balance claims about force compositions (e.g. melee vs shooting armies) are usually anecdotal; a simulator can only answer them if it demonstrably implements the rules and its experiments control for list selection, seat order and opponent quality.

## What I built

I built a rule-numbered conformance ledger and 42 seeded test suites, reachability audits that catch implemented rules no driver can call, and record-and-replay determinism as a conformance oracle. On top of that sit round-robin list tournaments with seats swapped, Bradley-Terry strength with bootstrap intervals, head-to-head policy duels with A/A and inverted positive controls, and power calculations run before any tuning.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What it is for

Mirrors combat-model verification and force-on-force analysis: how a plausible headline can be a sample-selection artifact, how a silent input substitution biases every batch result, and how positive and negative controls bound what a simulation study can conclude.
:::

## Tools

JavaScript (Node >=18, no dependencies), Python 3 (serve, data build, RL bridge with numpy), Bradley-Terry / bootstrap, Wilson intervals, Seeded PRNG record/replay

[A simulator of a tabletop ruleset, built as a testbed for rules-engine verification and Monte Carlo experiment design.]{.fine}
